examples: You have ten sessions open and the computer is slowing down: sleep the ones you are not using today.
Before a long break, sleep a session instead of closing it, so you can pick the conversation up exactly where it stopped.
Mark a session unread before sleeping it overnight; tomorrow its green moon reminds you to come back to it.
how_to: Open the session's menu (three dots on its drawer row) and choose sleep agent.
The agent stops and its terminal closes; the row stays where it was, showing a moon.
To bring it back, open the same menu and choose wake agent. It resumes the same conversation.
A session whose agent exited on its own (/exit, Ctrl-C or a crash) also shows a moon. Wake brings it back in its own terminal, resuming the same conversation; nothing running is stopped.
To discard a sleeping agent for good, choose kill agent on its row and confirm. The record leaves your lists and cannot be woken; the conversation history is kept.
To keep a reminder, mark the session unread before or after sleeping it: the moon then shows in the unread green, and the flag is still there after you wake it.

When something scheduled will wake a sleeping session (a Task Manager item with a fire time or a repeat that tells it, or an automation aimed at it that wakes it), a small clock sits beside its sleeping mark; hover it for the next wake time.

name: Sleep a session
summary: put a running session to sleep to free up resources without losing its conversation.
where: Open the agents drawer on the left.
Open a claude or codex session's menu with the three dots on its row.
An asleep session keeps its row and shows a moon in place of its light.
A moon in the unread green is an asleep session you flagged for follow-up.
